editorialRejections.title: EU Parliament Calls for Release of Burchuladze, ‘All Political Prisoners’ in New Georgia Resolution
editorialRejections.summary: Up to 64 people were charged and eventually convicted over the October 4 unrest in Georgia
editorialRejections.body: The European Parliament has adopted a resolution titled “Case of Paata Burchuladze and political prisoners under the Georgian Dream regime,” calling for the “immediate and unconditional release” of renowned Georgian opera singer Paata Burchuladze and two opposition politicians, Irakli Nadiradze and Paata Manjgaladze, who are currently serving seven-year prison sentences in connection with the October 4, 2025 election-day unrest, as well as other "political prisoners." Up to 64 people were charged and eventually convicted over the October 4 unrest in Georgia. Many secured early release through plea bargains or presidential pardons. Around 19 remain behind bars, while four are expected to be released in the coming weeks. 24/11/2026 - Georgia’s Protest Arrests: Who Remains Behind Bars? The resolution was adopted on November 26, with 441 MEPs voting in favor, 47 against, and 86 abstaining. The vote was preceded by a debate held a day earlier, during which 14 of the 15 MEPs who took the floor criticized the ruling Georgian Dream party. French MEP Thierry Mariani, of the far-right Patriots group, was the sole exception defending the Georgian authorities. The resolution also renewed calls for sanctions against the ruling party founder Bidzina Ivanishvili, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, Disputed Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili, Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze, "and other senior officials, as well as judges, prosecutors and law enforcement officials." 26/10/2026 - Opposition Alliance Launches Protest Campaign With Tbilisi Rally Amid Party Ban Proceedings Resolution in Detail The resolution says Burchuladze, 71, a Georgian-Austrian citizen and "a prominent opera singer and civic activist who has made an outstanding contribution to Georgian and European culture," was sentenced to seven years in prison in May 2026, "on politically motivated charges." The document says that "grave concerns persist" regarding the fairness of Burchuladze's proceedings, "the proportionality of the sentence and his detention conditions, including prolonged isolation, severely restricted contact with the outside world and inadequate medical care, given his age and health." It views Burchuladze's case "against the backdrop of growing Russian influence and systematic erosion of democracy, judicial independence and fundamental freedoms, where the regime systematically weaponizes the judiciary and state institutions to silence dissent, journalists and civil society." The resolution further states that "the crackdown on peaceful protesters and the misuse of restrictive legislation to curtail fundamental freedoms are fundamentally incompatible with the Georgian people’s European aspirations and Georgia’s obligations under the EU-Georgia Association Agreement," reiterating that the EP "has repeatedly condemned the persecution of political opponents and called for the immediate release of all prisoners of conscience." Under the adopted first amendment, the document "strongly condemns the conviction of Paata Burchuladze, Irakli Nadiradze and Paata Manjgaladze; calls for their immediate and unconditional release, along with all political prisoners and illegally detained persons, irrespective of their political affiliation, in particular former President Mikheil Saakashvili, Giorgi Baramidze, Nika Melia, Elene Khoshtaria and Mzia Amaglobeli, and all peaceful protesters in detention." It demands that the EP members be granted "unhindered access to those detained," and "holds the Georgian authorities fully responsible for their life, health and safety," calling for "immediate, unhindered access to independent doctors for the detainees." It calls on the “self-appointed” Georgian authorities to “fully respect international fair-trial standards” and guarantee Burchuladze access to adequate medical care, legal assistance, and regular contact with his family. It also calls for full respect for his right to unhindered consular access. The resolution further urges the authorities to end “the politically motivated prosecution and judicial harassment of artists, opposition figures, journalists and activists, and to guarantee full freedom of expression, assembly and association.” It also calls for "independent investigations into allegations of excessive use of force, intimidation and mistreatment of protesters, and for those responsible to be held accountable under the law." Reaffirming its “unwavering support for the Georgian people and their democratic aspirations,” the European Parliament stresses that respect for the rule of law, the European Convention on Human Rights and fundamental rights is "indispensable to any progress towards EU accession." Under its adopted second amendment, the resolution also “regrets” the failure of “certain” EU Member States to hold those responsible for Georgia’s democratic backsliding accountable. It urges the bloc to maintain a “coordinated response” and reiterates its call for "targeted sanctions, including asset freezes and an EU entry and transit ban, against those responsible for undermining democracy, the rule of law, as well as serious human rights violations, in particular Bidzina Ivanishvili, Irakli Kobakhidze, Shalva Papuashvili, Kakha Kaladze and other senior officials, as well as judges, prosecutors and law enforcement officials." The resolution concludes by instructing the European Parliament’s President to forward the document to the Council, the European Commission, the High Representative, EU Member States and the “self-appointed Georgian authorities.” November 25 Debates Rasa Juknevičienė, Lithuanian MEP (Group of the European People's Party): "Paata Burchuladze is one of the great voices of European opera. Today he is 71 and he is in prison, sentenced to seven years for standing with the Georgian people. He is not alone. Last week I met with family members of Georgian political prisoners. They told us about terrible prison conditions. Today I met Nini Manjaladze, whose father was sentenced alongside Burchuladze. Nini is here with us in the gallery tonight. She told us that her father shares a sixteen square meter cell with five other prisoners. He sent us a message from prison: Europe is Georgia's home. He also thanked the European Parliament for supporting those fighting for Georgia's freedom. Many other prisoners are young people whose criminal records could affect their entire lives, making it harder for them to study and find work. We must help them. This Saturday marks two years of Georgian daily protesting for their European future. Let us be as stubborn as they are and impose sanctions on those responsible for taking away Georgia's future." Tobias Cremer, German MEP (Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats): "Paata Burchuladze has become famous through the power of his voice as one of Georgia's most celebrated opera singers. His voice has filled opera houses from Vienna to New York. But today his own government is trying to silence that voice by locking him away on fabricated charges. His crime? Daring to speak out against a regime that is trying to turn Georgia from a European democracy into a Belarusian-style regime under the shadow of the Kremlin. But Paata is not alone. Eighty percent of Georgians still want a European future. And for almost exactly two years now they have been going on the streets for that. [...] Impose targeted sanctions on Ivanishvili and keep up the pressure on this regime until the voice of Paata and the voices of all Georgians can once again ring out freely and loudly in a democratic and a European Georgia. " Małgorzata Gosiewska, Polish MEP (European Conservatives and Reformists Group): "How many more Georgians must be imprisoned? How many sentences must be handed down before the EU takes effective action? [...] Georgia has changed its course. It now turns towards Russian influence, becomes a place of circumvention of sanctions and the flow of illegal capital. And its democracy is systematically strangled. It's time to end the declarations. I demand personal sanctions against Ivanishvili's family and his political and business circle. An asset freeze and a travel ban to the EU. Let's not allow Russian interests to win in Georgia against the will of its citizens [...]." Villy Søvndal, Danish MEP (Group of the Greens/European Free Alliance): "The past EU membership may seem long, but at a time when the regime is trying to push the Georgian people further away from Europe, it's more important than ever that we as Europeans do not turn our back on them. We have a responsibility to support the Georgian people's fight for freedom and democracy. That is why EU member states must condemn violations of fundamental rights and hold the regime accountable for Georgia's democratic backsliding." Nacho Sánchez Amor, Spanish MEP (Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats): "At this stage, the only thing that will work is sanctions, but sanctions only seem to work if it's Georgia linked with Russia. But what about supporting democracy? We need a basket of sanctions targeting oligarchs in Georgia, even if we do not secure unanimity and we should publicize names of any governments that refuse to support this." Michał Szczerba, Polish MEP (EPP) "In Georgia today, being pro-European can land you in prison. On contrary, being linked to the Iranian regime, currently, apparently, is not a problem. Paata Burchuladze, a world-famous opera singer, is behind bars. His crime? Standing up for European Georgia. European NGOs are being driven out, while organizations linked to the Iran's Revolutionary Guard operate freely. [...] Georgia drifts towards Moscow and Tehran, and it is a disaster for the Georgian people, a victory for Russia and geopolitical defeat for the European Union. We must not allow that to happen." Dainius Žalimas, Lithuanian MEP (Renew Europe Group): "Today at least 55 political prisoners remain behind bars, while dozens of defendants have been pressured into admitting guilt. What we are witnessing is the systemic dismantling of political pluralism and the establishment of a one-party system. With the judiciary being instrumentalized to suppress political opposition and civil society. [...] EU must pursue a coordinated policy of non-recognition of the Georgian Dream regime and impose targeted sanctions not only on its political leadership but also on judges, prosecutors, law enforcement officials responsible for human rights violations, both who instrumentalize justice for political repression must face personal consequences." Thierry Mariani, French MEP (Patriots for Europe Group): "Fourth October of 2025, Pata Buruladze and his friends declared a legitimate the Georgian government, and yet its democratically elected. They then called on the police to disobey. And they encouraged the crowd to enter the building of the presidential palace. These seditious calls were an attempt to overthrow the constitutional order, leaving many seriously injured among the forces of law and order in Georgia. And Georgian justice, independent and sovereign, judged what it considered a case of an assault on the fundamental interests of the nation, rather like the rush on the Capitol, the sitting judgment of thousands of rioters. Yet Europe said nothing about that." editorialRejections.title: Russia responds after Trump and NATO chief tell Putin not to widen war
editorialRejections.body:
The Kremlin has responded to a statement from Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte this morning, in which they warned Vladimir Putin not to widen the war.

When asked about the statement, spokesperson Dmitry Peskov instead pointed the blame at Kyiv, saying:

"As to the expansion of the Ukrainian conflict, this probably means the attempts of the Kyiv regime to expand the conflict geography. We are observing terrorist activity of the Kyiv regime in the Mediterranean and the Baltic Sea. This is bound to raise concern primarily among coastal nations but also, most likely, within the North Atlantic Alliance as a whole."

Peskov's comments were in reference to recent successful attacks on Russian ships in Libya and the Gulf of Finland.

The Kremlin also repeated its often-heard line, saying Ukraine is now less inclined towards peace due to European encouragement.

editorialRejections.title: Russia should not expand the war, Trump and NATO chief say in statement
editorialRejections.body:
Russia should avoid any actions that risk expanding its war in Ukraine, Donald Trump and the NATO chief have said in a joint statement.

Trump met Mark Rutte yesterday in Florida, a week after calling Vladimir Putin his "friend" at a summit in China.

"We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," they said in their statement.

Rutte has repeatedly tried to soothe tension within NATO ​and keep Trump onside. He said it is normal for major ​nuclear powers to meet.

The pair also talked about boosting defence spending and investment in the US and across NATO, according to their statement.

editorialRejections.title: Several countries slam suspected Iranian attack on Kuwait
editorialRejections.summary: A number of countries and their officials have condemned the latest drone attacks launched against Kuwait, which killed two Italian nationals
editorialRejections.body: A number of countries and their officials have condemned the latest drone attacks launched against Kuwait, which killed two Italian nationals. The UK minister Stephen Doughty condemned the attack as "utterly unacceptable" and said that his country "stands firmly with Kuwait, Italy and all those affected, without making mention of who could be behind the attacks. The Syrian Foreign Ministry slammed Iran for the strikes, and affirmed its "full solidarity" with Kuwait. It also extended its condolences to the families of those killed. Similarly, Saudi Arabia has also pinned the attacks on Iran, saying: "The continued Iranian attacks further exacerbate tensions and undermine stability." Iran has denied the allegations that it launched the drones on Kuwait, with Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi calling the incident "suspicious".
